Evidence: Allah is described in the Qurʾān as the one and only God, unique, omnipotent, and all-merciful (Source 1). The Qurʾān emphasizes Allah's singularity and sole sovereignty, known as tawḥīd (Source 2). Allah is seen as the creator and sustainer of the universe, and Muslims believe that He can grant requests and bestow blessings according to His will (Source 3). The Qurʾān contains 99 names that reflect Allah's attributes, including The Merciful and The All-Knowing, indicating His power and mercy (Source 1).
Justification: The retrieved evidence directly supports the claim that Allah is capable of granting prayers and is all-powerful. It states that Allah is unique, omnipotent, and all-merciful, which aligns with the assertion that He can bestow blessings according to His will. The Qurʾān's emphasis on Allah's attributes and His role as the creator further corroborates the claim, as mentioned in Sources 1, 2, and 3.
